vignette: Aisha, a 25-year-old African-American nurse, has been grappling with profound psychological distress since her time spent in a war-torn region. The trauma she experienced there has left deep scars on both her psyche and professional life. Aisha was deployed to provide medical care during an intense period of conflict when civilians were caught in the crossfire. One particularly harrowing incident involved treating a child who had been severely injured by shrapnel. Despite her best efforts, the child did not survive. This event triggered a cascade of emotional responses that have since permeated every aspect of Aisha's life. The memory of the child's suffering and death is seared into Aisha’s mind. When she thinks about it, she feels as though she is reliving those moments; the sounds of gunfire, the smell of blood, and the sense of helplessness are all too real. This overwhelming emotional intensity forces her to stop whatever she is doing, often in the middle of a shift at the hospital where she now works. She finds herself struggling to function when these memories flood back, and the grief becomes so intense that it leaves her numb. Aisha has come to believe that what happened was not only devastating but also deeply humiliating. She feels inadequate for not being able to save the child, and this inadequacy has led her to perceive herself as fundamentally defective. These negative appraisals have become a constant presence in her life. To cope with these overwhelming feelings of humiliation and inadequacy, Aisha has developed several maladaptive strategies. One of these is retreating into her own world through fantasies where she can escape the harsh realities of her memories. When things get too much to bear, she drifts off into a space where none of this pain exists. She also avoids talking about what happened with others or even thinking about it herself, believing that confronting these thoughts will only bring more distress and humiliation. The avoidance behaviors have started to take a toll on Aisha’s work as a nurse. She finds herself avoiding patients who remind her of the child she lost, which has strained her relationships with colleagues and supervisors. Her performance at work has declined, leading to several close calls that could have jeopardized patient care. As the memories continue to haunt her, they feed into her negative appraisals, creating a cycle that feels impossible to break. Each time she relives the event, the feelings of inadequacy and humiliation intensify, driving her deeper into avoidance behaviors. This cycle has left Aisha feeling increasingly isolated and hopeless. What finally brought Aisha to seek help was an incident where she almost made a critical error at work due to being mentally absent from the moment. She realized that her coping strategies were no longer sustainable and that they were putting herself and others at risk. Despite her fears, Aisha is hopeful that therapy might provide some relief from the overwhelming emotions and allow her to regain control over her life. In seeking help, Aisha hopes for a way to process these memories without being overwhelmed by them, to feel less inadequate, and to reconnect with her profession in a meaningful way. Her journey towards healing has just begun, but she is determined not to let her past define her future.
